verdict.rationale: Docs describe a driver Registry that eliminates hand-written drivers, a quick first-machine wizard/install flow, hardware model search, uniform component APIs so code doesn't break when hardware changes, built-in test panels/keyboard control for immediate motion without deploying code, and a motion-planning service for collision-free moves — directly matching drivers+config+first-motion in short order. Community evidence corroborates the architecture (gRPC, open-source RDK) and offline-tolerant operation, though one experienced roboticist expresses skepticism about fit for industrial use cases (not a concrete contradiction of bring-up speed). Missing for 10: independent/hands-on timing evidence validating the 'hours not weeks' claim and confirmation the driver registry covers a broad enough range of real-world hardware.
